minutes.headline: Water commissioners opened truck bids and heard the Pond View 40B developer's water-line plan; no votes except adjournment.
minutes.summary: The board opened bids for a new truck and took them under advisement until the absent member returns. Most of the meeting was developer Kevin O'Brien presenting a conceptual water (and sewer) layout for Pond View Estates under a 40B permit, with discussion of a booster pump, a storage tank, district boundaries and legal questions. The board agreed to ask its attorneys questions and to meet again after the ZBA acts; the meeting then adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Water District board opened bids for a new truck and took them under advisement until the absent commissioner returns.
A developer presented a conceptual water and sewer layout for Pond View Estates, a 40B project, including a booster pump, a storage tank and wells.
The board will ask its attorney whether a storage tank can be located outside the water district.
The board will consult its attorneys, possibly with the town attorney, on the ZBA's authority over the water district under 40B.
The developer is to return with the fire department after the ZBA approves the project to work out final design; the only vote was adjournment.

why_it_matters: A 40B project can ask the water district to serve a large new development, and who pays for the pump, tank and pipe, and who has authority over the system, are still undecided.
The truck purchase is undecided, so the cost to ratepayers (aluminum or steel body, bid or state purchasing) will come back for a later vote.
watch_next: The ZBA's action on the Pond View 40B permit, after which the developer is to return to the board.
The board's decision on the truck bids once the absent commissioner returns, and its attorneys' answers on the tank and ZBA authority.
